The lazy-loading path is `getAsyncLifecycle` in `esm-react-utils`, which wraps a dynamic `import()` and only builds the single-spa lifecycle once that promise resolves. Its docs are in `esm-framework/docs`.

**How it works**

1. A module's `index.ts` exports a lifecycle built with `getAsyncLifecycle(() => import('./some.component'), options)`. The `import()` is not evaluated at module load, so the component's code stays out of the initial bundle. Example: `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/index.ts:118-123` and `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-form-engine-app/src/index.ts:49`.
2. `getAsyncLifecycle` returns a function, `() => lazy().then(({ default: Component }) => getLifecycle(Component, options))`. The import runs only when single-spa asks for the lifecycle, which is when the page or extension is activated (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/getLifecycle.ts:52-57`).
3. `getLifecycle` wraps the component with `openmrsComponentDecorator` (error boundaries, config, extension support) and passes it to `singleSpaReact` (`getLifecycle.ts:26-32`).
4. `getSyncLifecycle` is the non-lazy variant for components already in memory (`getLifecycle.ts:77-79`). `getAsyncExtensionLifecycle` is a deprecated alias of `getAsyncLifecycle` (`getLifecycle.ts:84`).
5. For extension slots, `renderExtension` mounts a lazily loaded component from any module into a DOM node. It looks up the registration and uses its `load` function (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-extensions/src/render.ts:369-381`). I did not read the body past line 401, so I have not verified how `load` is called.
